claims.text: TaVCrW is considered as a random solid solution with a BCC solid phase and a liquid phase, with possible SRO in the solid.
Replacing EAM and TI with an MTP-FEP workflow will reduce computational cost by more than 80%.
The MTP-FEP workflow will maintain sub-meV free-energy accuracy for melting-point prediction.
A DFT-trained MTP can accurately reproduce the ab initio phase-space distributions of solid and liquid TaVCrW.
Accurate reproduction of the ab initio phase-space distribution provides sufficient distribution overlap to replace TI with FEP.
FEP accuracy depends on phase-space overlap between the reference and target states.
An MTP trained on DFT has a sufficiently accurate potential-energy surface to provide the overlap needed for perturbative free-energy calculation.
The MTP captures electronic and vibrational entropy contributions that EAM potentials miss.
The SRO contribution to the solid-liquid free-energy difference in TaVCrW is negligible near 2000-2400 K.
In MoNbTaW, the SRO-induced strengthening effect on screw-dislocation mobility diminishes with temperature and becomes negligible at 2000 K.
The attenuation of SRO effects on dislocation mobility in MoNbTaW implies negligible SRO free-energy stabilization in TaVCrW near melting.
A liquid supercell containing more than 500 atoms is required to avoid finite-size effects and converge FEP.
A solid supercell containing at least 1000 atoms is required to capture SRO if it is present.
Multiple overlapping FEP windows ensure adequate overlap of phase-space distributions.
Outside 2000-2400 K, SRO effects in the TaVCrW solid may become significant again and require explicit modeling.
MTP evaluation is less computationally expensive than on-the-fly DFT sampling in TI.
FEP converges faster than TI for high-entropy systems when phase-space overlap is adequate.
The proposed method will predict the TaVCrW melting temperature within 10 K of approximately 2150 K.
The MTP-FEP solid-liquid free-energy difference will have uncertainty below 0.5 meV/atom.
The baseline TOR-TILD workflow costs more than ten times as much as the proposed method.

contradictions.description: The intervention says that EAM is replaced by the MTP, whereas the mechanism describes FEP overlap between an EAM reference and an MTP/DFT target. It is therefore unclear whether EAM remains the FEP reference or is removed from the workflow.
